operatorApproval.notes: The audit's earlier integrity scans were one-off scripts: they counted records, recomputed canonical hashes and listed dangling evidence paths, but they could not answer the question the X-series exposed - whether a fresh clone can walk the chain at all, since the record schema has no parent pointer and the chain is forward-only (parent.nextTaskId + parent.nextBaseSha must name a child record with that taskId and baseSha). The scanner ranks generations (out-chain > out-final > out-corrected > later corrections > out, negative-control generations scanned but never canonical) and separates canonical offenders from superseded history. On a clean checkout of the X-series tip it reports 87 records, 87 canonical-hash matches, 87 field-conforming, 55 forward links resolved and 8 offenders: five X-series chain parents naming a child while untracked - the conclude flow emits a chain generation after amending the evidence commit that would carry it, so those records only ever reached the working tree - and three historical (E02's negative-control generation names an E03 base no record carries, FIX-2 names FIX-3 whose record was never emitted, T09 names T10, a task the plan never contained). This unit commits those chain records and reports the residue honestly instead of rewriting the historical PASS records that produce it. | CHAIN CORRECTION: this record supersedes X07/out/X07.handoff.json (sha256 kept immutable in out/), whose nextBaseSha pointed at the task commit 548c2a83d041 while the next unit is cut from the evidence commit a17a48ecd4fd that carries this unit's record; code, proofs and scope are unchanged.
